ἐπὶ τῶν κτηνῶν· πρόβατα, φησὶν, ἦν αὐτῷ μύρια τε τρακισχίλια, ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀρχῇ
εἶχεν ἑπτα κισχίλια· καμήλων ἑξακισχίλια, ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀρχῇ εἶχεν τρισχίλια· ζεῦγα
βοῶν χίλια, πρῶτον γὰρ ἦσαν πεντακόσια. Τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν νομάδων ὄνων. 389
Γεννῶνται δὲ αὐτῷ, φησὶν, υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυγατέρες τρεῖς, ὅσοι ἦσαν καὶ πρότερον·
ἔδει δὲ τοὺς μὲν δεκατέσσαρας εἶναι, τὰς δὲ ἓξ, ἵνα εἶεν διπλοῖ τῶν ἀπολωλότων
παίδων. Λέ γομεν οὖν, ὅτι τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἀπολώλον ται, καὶ τὰ κτήνη· οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ καὶ
αἱ θυγα τέρες τεθνήκασιν, οὐκ ἀπώλοντο. Ἔδωκεν οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ἕτερα
τοσοῦτα τέκνα, ὥστε ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει διπλᾶ ἔχειν αὐτὰ, ὥστε καὶ πατέρα διπλασίων
παίδων αὐτὸν πεποίηκεν ὁ Θεὸς, ὧν ἦν πρότερον πατήρ. Εἰ δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ ἐσβέννυτο
μετὰ θάνατον, καὶ τὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως οὐκ ἦν ἀληθῶς, ἔδει υἱοὺς δοθῆναι
δεκατέσσαρας καὶ θυγατέρας ἕξ. ∆ιὸ ἱερῶς ἡ γραφὴ τετήρηκε περὶ τοῦ ὅτι ἔλαβεν
υἱοὺς ζʹ· εἰ δὲ ἐγεγόνεισαν αὐτῷ δέκα τέσσαρες υἱοὶ καὶ θυγατέρες ἓξ, σω ζομένου

pass_a_gloss: affliction, as the holy writing says, it was necessary for the children to be doubly. For look upon the cattle. Sheep, it says, were to him myriads three thousand, for in the beginning he had seven thousand. Camels six thousand, for in the beginning he had three thousand. Yokes of oxen a thousand, for first they were five hundred. The same also upon the donkeys. Are born to him, it says, seven sons and three daughters, as many as were before. It was necessary for the fourteen to be [children], and the six, so that they might be double of the lost children. Let us say then, that the sheep are lost, and the cattle. The sons and the daughters have died, they were not lost. Therefore God gave him other children so many, so that in the resurrection he might have double, so that God made him father of double children, of whom he was before father. If the soul is extinguished with death, and the resurrection things are not truly, it was necessary to give fourteen sons and six daughters. Therefore the holy writing kept [the text] concerning that he received sons six. If indeed he became to him fourteen sons and six daughters, while the word about the resurrection was being spoken, they are not given to him double, but triple, or were first. 1. And Job lived after the affliction one hundred seventy years, and all the years he lived two hundred forty. How is Job considered to have lived after the affliction one hundred seventy, of all the years of his life two hundred forty? We say therefore, being precise, that having received all the good things double, if even the years of the former prosperity are doubled, thus to count beforehand. He lived in the former prosperity one hundred twenty, and from when he received the affliction, he remained in the suffering one hundred forty. Thus the after the affliction is to be understood, not from when the affliction ceased, but from when it began. After the four and ten years, the time of the sickness,
pass_b_english: The text states that affliction required children to be doubled. Observe the livestock: sheep numbered thirty thousand, having begun with seven thousand. Camels totaled six thousand, starting with three thousand. Oxen yokes reached a thousand, initially five hundred. The same pattern applied to donkeys. Sons and daughters born to him totaled ten, matching his previous count. Fourteen children were necessary, along with six, to equal the number of lost offspring. We conclude that sheep and cattle were lost, while sons and daughters died but were not lost. Thus, God granted him an equal number of new children, ensuring double in the resurrection. This made him a father of double the children he once had. If souls perished with death and resurrection were false, fourteen sons and six daughters would have been required. The sacred text preserves the account of him receiving six sons. If he later had fourteen sons and six daughters while discussing resurrection, the children would be tripled rather than doubled, contradicting their original number.

Job lived one hundred seventy years after the affliction, with his total lifespan reaching two hundred forty. How does this align with his entire life span? Precisely: having received double blessings, even the years of former prosperity are counted doubly. He lived one hundred twenty years in prosperity, then one hundred forty in suffering. The period 'after the affliction' refers not to when it ended but when it began. Following four and ten years of illness, the duration of his suffering is noted.

choices.choice: Rendered as 'doubly' to emphasize symbolic multiplicity over literal numerical doubling
Used 'cattle' to align with the specific ancient context of pastoral wealth
Omitted explicit biblical citations to maintain focus on the text's internal logic
